stem:
Qadir has a square of side 3 cm. He makes a new square whose side is 6 cm, so the side length is multiplied by 2.

Which statement about the area is correct?

options.text: The area becomes 2 times as large, matching the side factor.
The area stays the same because both figures are still squares.
The area becomes 4 times as large, because area scales with the square of the side factor.
The perimeter becomes 4 times as large, and that same factor rule applies to area.

teacher.key_rationale: Area of a square is s², so multiplying the side by 2 multiplies the area by 4. Matching the side factor 2 is surface capture; saying area is unchanged omits the side-change condition; treating perimeter scaling as the area rule is a scope error.

mx_swap.reason: Diagonal-doubling construction invents a diagonal not in the stem; kept surface_feature_capture, condition_omission, scope_error.
